title: SLO Rollout Field Lab: Kickstart Agenda and Decision Log
content:
Document purpose:
This doc captures the kickstart plan, agenda, sprint canvas and early decision log for the SLO Rollout Field Lab. Goal is to run a time-boxed, cross-functional pilot that proves our SLO governance and rollout mechanics across hosted API and Dedicated surface areas, then produce repeatable playbooks for broader adoption.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We are launching a 6-week Field Lab with three product teams to validate an SLO lifecycle: define service level objectives, instrument telemetry and alerts, run canary and canary-to-global rollouts, and exercise incident-to-policy closure (error budget driven). Outcomes: validated dashboards and alerts, one automated canary pipeline, runbook templates, and a decision log capturing tradeoffs. Next steps after the lab will be a refined SLO playbook and onboarding kit for 10+ teams in Q4.

Objectives (measurable):
- Establish clear SLO definitions for 3 services (hosted-generate, embeddings-batch, routing-proxy) by EOW week 1.
- Verify telemetry coverage: latency, error rate, key business signals (tokens/req) and request provenance for 100% of canary traffic by week 2.
- Complete 3 canary rollouts (one per service) with automated rollback on error budget burn > 20% in 1 hour by week 4.
- Produce a template runbook, oncall pairing checklist, and incident->SLO retrospective workflow by end of week 6.

Scope (in):
- Pilot limited to: hosted API generation endpoint (model-gen v2), embeddings-batch v1, request-routing-proxy.
- Use of Redwood Console dashboards and tracing hooks; add temporary sampling rules where needed.
- Canary automation via existing release pipeline (PLAT-221) with minor scripting.

Out of scope (explicit):
- Dedicated capacity SLA guarantees and contractual changes (those follow in a separate track).
- Model quality regressions and evals (handled by Model Onboarding/Research).

Stakeholders and roles (RACI-lite):
- Project lead / owner: Maya Lin (SRE) — coordination, decision log owner.
- Product partners: Sylvia Cortez (Hosted API PM), Ravi Patel (Optimize PM) — define business impact metrics.
- Observability: Ethan Jacobs (Observability Eng) — dashboard ownership and instrumentation tasks.
- Release automation: Naomi Okafor (Platform Eng) — pipeline and rollback automation.
- Oncall pairing / test operators: feature-team SREs (Liam O'Neill and two rotating engineers) — execute canaries and postmortems.

High-level timeline (6-week cadence):
- Week 0 (pre-kick): Align on scope, grant telemetry access, and set up sandbox orgs.
- Week 1: Define SLOs, measurement windows (p95/p99 decisions), and acceptance thresholds.
- Week 2: Implement missing metrics, create dashboard mockups, baseline error budgets.
- Week 3: Canary automation dry-run in staging, tabletop for rollback triggers.
- Week 4: Execute first canary (hosted-gen), collect signals and iterate.
- Week 5: Execute second/third canaries, consolidate runbooks.
- Week 6: Wrap-up, publish playbook + handover to Reliability Enablement.

Kickstart agenda (first 90 minutes):
- 00:00–00:10: Welcome, outcomes and guardrails (Maya)
- 00:10–00:25: Quick service profiles (product owners): traffic patterns, top user flows, business impact 
- 00:25–00:45: Proposed SLOs per service and measurement window rationale (Ethan + Sylvia)
- 00:45–01:00: Observability gaps and instrumentation plan (Ethan)
- 01:00–01:15: Canary automation approach and rollback contracts (Naomi)
- 01:15–01:25: Communications and oncall pairing plan (Liam)
- 01:25–01:30: Immediate next actions and owners (Maya)

Decision log (running):
- 2026-08-12 — D001 — Measurement window: Use p95 latency for canary gating, use p99 for long-term SLO. Rationale: p95 is more stable for quick canary decisions; p99 will be the customer-facing SLO. (Decided by: Maya, Ethan, Sylvia)
- 2026-08-16 — D002 — Error budget policy: fast-fail canary at 20% burn in 1 hour, staggered rollback at 10% burn sustained for 30 minutes during staged rollout. (Decided by: Naomi, Maya)
- 2026-08-19 — D003 — Synthetic probes: 1 probe region per major cloud region, 30s cadence, sample with production headers. (Decided by: Observability + Product)
- 2026-08-24 — D004 — Alerting thresholds: firing at 5% of error budget consumed in 15m; paging only if >10% in 15m. (Decided by: SRE leads)

Acceptance criteria for field lab success:
- Telemetry: All SLO signals (p95/p99, error rate, request count, provenance) emitted and visible in Console dashboards.
- Runbook: One tested runbook per service that includes rollback steps, communication templates and postmortem prompts.
- Automation: Canary pipeline can perform a rollback automatically within 5 minutes of trigger detection.
- Knowledge transfer: One 60-minute training session delivered to Reliability Enablement with materials published.

Telemetry and dashboards checklist:
- Confirm metric names and tags: service.name, deployment.env, model.version, route.name.
- Add business tags to telemetry for attribution (customer_tier, route_group).
- Baseline capture: 10 days of historical data ingested for threshold calculation.
- Dashboards: SLO summary tile, error budget burn chart, canary vs prod comparison, traces sampled at 10% for failed requests.

Runbook sketch (fields to capture):
- Runbook title; service owner; SLOs and escalation thresholds; how to read the SLO tile; typical causes; immediate mitigations; how to trigger rollback; stakeholder comm templates; postmortem checklist.

Communication plan (who says what, when):
- Canary start: slack alert to #sre-ops, #product-hosted-api with canary link and expected duration.
- If rollback triggered: page SRE oncall and notify product leads with templated message.
- Post-canary summary: publish to Confluence Field Lab page + short TL;DR to leadership mailing list.

Open questions and risks:
- Q1: Are current traces sufficiently high-fidelity to diagnose tail-latency root causes quickly? (Owner: Ethan)
- Q2: Do feature teams accept p99 SLOs as primary customer promise, or prefer p95? (Owner: Sylvia)
- Risk A: Incomplete tagging could make attribution noisy; mitigation: temporary tagging enforcement gate in pipeline.
- Risk B: Error budget model surprises for teams used to unconstrained deploy cadence; mitigation: paired oncall + sandboxed cadence for first two rollouts.

Resource asks (asks to leadership / platform):
- One week of Observability Eng time (Ethan) prioritized weeks 1–2 to close instrumentation gaps.
- 0.2 FTE release-engineer (Naomi) for automation scripting during weeks 2–5.
- Temporary increase in trace sampling to 10% for canary windows.

Checklists for canary day (preflight):
- Verify metric ingestion for last 24h
- Run pipeline dry-run in staging and confirm rollback signal fires in <5m
- Confirm oncall pairing rota and phone/pager escalation listed in runbook
- Publish scheduled window and expected user impact to #infra-alerts

Postmortem / retro expectations:
- If an error budget breach happened during a canary, produce a short postmortem within 72h with: timeline, root cause hypothesis, why SLO gating failed/succeeded, action items, ownership and expected completion dates.
- Maintain the decision log as the single source of truth for tradeoffs and rationale; decisions must include date, decision id, rationale, owners.

Next actions (initial):
- Maya: finalize kickoff agenda and invite distribution list (due 2026-08-13).
- Ethan: run a telemetry gap scan and list missing metrics (due 2026-08-14).
- Naomi: prototype rollback hook in a sandbox pipeline and report back with ETA (due 2026-08-18).
- Sylvia: provide business impact scoring for the three selected services (due 2026-08-14).

Appendix: quick reference SLO examples (templates)
- Hosted-Generate (customer-facing SLO): 99th percentile request latency < 350ms over 30d; objective stated as p99 < 350ms; alert if 10% error budget consumed in 1d.
- Embeddings-Batch (internal job SLO): 95th percentile latency < 3s for batch-cron windows; objective p95 < 3s; paging only for >50% of scheduled runs failing.
- Routing-Proxy (availability): Availability > 99.95% monthly; error budget carryover rules documented in policy.

Document ownership and maintenance:
- This file is the living kickoff artifact for the SLO Field Lab; Maya Lin is the decision log owner and will update entries as decisions are made. After the lab, this content will be folded into the Reliability Enablement playbook and archived with final outcomes.
